opening.text: Imagine an old house that stood for centuries. Over time, parts were lost. A wall fell. A roof gave way. Then one day the owner sends builders to bring it back, the way it was first drawn. That is the Restoration. God did not patch an old house. He restored what He built.

mainMessage.text: The Restoration is God bringing back the gospel of Jesus Christ, the priesthood and His Church. He did it through a young prophet, and He is still doing it today.

blocks.text: **The Restoration was promised** God told His prophets this day would come. Peter spoke of it. Amos spoke of the hunger that came before it.

Repent ye therefore, and be converted, that your sins may be blotted out, when the times of refreshing shall come from the presence of the Lord; And he shall send Jesus Christ, which before was preached unto you: Whom the heaven must receive until the times of restitution of all things, which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets since the world began.
Behold, the days come, saith the Lord God, that I will send a famine in the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the Lord:

The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in “The Restoration of the Fulness of the Gospel of Jesus Christ: A Bicentennial Proclamation to the World.” It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. President Russell M. Nelson read it at the April 2020 general conference.
We gladly declare that the promised Restoration goes forward through continuing revelation.
God promised it, and God keeps His promises.
**Why the house needed work** People lost truth over time. Paul warned about it. Isaiah described the dark.
Let no man deceive you by any means: for that day shall not come, except there come a falling away first, and that man of sin be revealed, the son of perdition;
For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
With reverence and gratitude, we as His Apostles invite all to know—as we do—that the heavens are open.
The dark did not stay. Light came back.
**A boy in a grove** Joseph Smith was fourteen. He asked God which church to join. God answered him in person.

It no sooner appeared than I found myself delivered from the enemy which held me bound. When the light rested upon me I saw two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description, standing above me in the air. One of them spake unto me, calling me by name and said, pointing to the other—This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!

I was answered that I must join none of them, for they were all wrong; and the Personage who addressed me said that all their creeds were an abomination in his sight; that those professors were all corrupt; that: “they draw near to me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me, they teach for doctrines the commandments of men, having a form of godliness, but they deny the power thereof.”
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
In humility, we declare that in answer to his prayer, God the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, appeared to Joseph.
The Father and the Son know us by name.
**A book from the dust** Moroni told Joseph about gold plates. The book on them holds the gospel as the Savior taught it.

He called me by name, and said unto me that he was a messenger sent from the presence of God to me, and that his name was Moroni; that God had a work for me to do; and that my name should be had for good and evil among all nations, kindreds, and tongues, or that it should be both good and evil spoken of among all people.

He said there was a book deposited, written upon gold plates, giving an account of the former inhabitants of this continent, and the source from whence they sprang. He also said that the fulness of the everlasting Gospel was contained in it, as delivered by the Savior to the ancient inhabitants;
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
It teaches of life's purpose and explains the doctrine of Christ, which is central to that purpose.
The book is not a side story. It points us to Christ.
**Authority came back** Words alone are not enough. God also gave authority to act in His name. Heavenly messengers gave it.

The keys of the kingdom of God are committed unto man on the earth, and from thence shall the gospel roll forth unto the ends of the earth, as the stone which is cut out of the mountain without hands shall roll forth, until it has filled the whole earth.
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
Three of the original twelve Apostles—Peter, James, and John—restored the apostleship and keys of priesthood authority.
A key opens a door. These keys open the way to God's ordinances.
**The Church built again** On April 6, 1830, the Church was organized. It is still growing, and it is for everyone.

And also those to whom these commandments were given, might have power to lay the foundation of this church, and to bring it forth out of obscurity and out of darkness, the only true and living church upon the face of the whole earth, with which I, the Lord, am well pleased, speaking unto the church collectively and not individually—

And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, organized on April 6, 1830, is Christ's New Testament Church restored.
The kingdom will stand, and there is a place in it for you.

story.title: Nehemiah rebuilds the wall

blocks.text: Jerusalem lay in ruins. Nehemiah did not wait for someone else. He called the people to rebuild.

Then said I unto them, Ye see the distress that we are in, how Jerusalem lieth waste, and the gates thereof are burned with fire: come, and let us build up the wall of Jerusalem, that we be no more a reproach. Then I told them of the hand of my God which was good upon me; as also the king’s words that he had spoken unto me. And they said, Let us rise up and build. So they strengthened their hands for this good work.
The people saw the ruin, and they also saw God's hand. We can do the same. We can see what was lost, and we can see what God has restored. Then we can help build.

story.title: The lost coin

blocks.text: A woman had ten coins and lost one. She would not give up.

Either what woman having ten pieces of silver, if she lose one piece, doth not light a candle, and sweep the house, and seek diligently till she find it? And when she hath found it, she calleth her friends and her neighbours together, saying, Rejoice with me; for I have found the piece which I had lost.
God searches for us the same way. The Restoration is part of that search. When we feel found, we want to call our friends and share the joy.

blocks.text: Jesus taught that His kingdom starts small.

Another parable put he forth unto them, saying, The kingdom of heaven is like to a grain of mustard seed, which a man took, and sowed in his field: Which indeed is the least of all seeds: but when it is grown, it is the greatest among herbs, and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and lodge in the branches thereof.
A prayer in a grove looked small. Look at the tree now. Your own faith can grow the same way, from a small seed to a place of shelter for others.

Moreover, thou son of man, take thee one stick, and write upon it, For Judah, and for the children of Israel his companions: then take another stick, and write upon it, For Joseph, the stick of Ephraim, and for all the house of Israel his companions: And join them one to another into one stick; and they shall become one in thine hand.
Many Latter-day Saints see the Bible and the Book of Mormon in this picture. Two records, one witness of Christ. They do not compete. They work together.

For, behold, the darkness shall cover the earth, and gross darkness the people: but the Lord shall arise upon thee, and his glory shall be seen upon thee.
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
With reverence and gratitude, we as His Apostles invite all to know—as we do—that the heavens are open.
The covering has been lifted.
**The first brushstroke** The work began when a boy knelt in a grove and God answered.

It no sooner appeared than I found myself delivered from the enemy which held me bound. When the light rested upon me I saw two Personages, whose brightness and glory defy all description, standing above me in the air. One of them spake unto me, calling me by name and said, pointing to the other—This is My Beloved Son. Hear Him!

I was answered that I must join none of them, for they were all wrong; and the Personage who addressed me said that all their creeds were an abomination in his sight; that those professors were all corrupt; that: “they draw near to me with their lips, but their hearts are far from me, they teach for doctrines the commandments of men, having a form of godliness, but they deny the power thereof.”
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
In humility, we declare that in answer to his prayer, God the Father and His Son, Jesus Christ, appeared to Joseph.
God does not need a perfect person. He needs a willing one.
**Colors that do not fade** The Book of Mormon shows the gospel in clear color. It came from plates Moroni guarded.

He called me by name, and said unto me that he was a messenger sent from the presence of God to me, and that his name was Moroni; that God had a work for me to do; and that my name should be had for good and evil among all nations, kindreds, and tongues, or that it should be both good and evil spoken of among all people.

He said there was a book deposited, written upon gold plates, giving an account of the former inhabitants of this continent, and the source from whence they sprang. He also said that the fulness of the everlasting Gospel was contained in it, as delivered by the Savior to the ancient inhabitants;
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
It teaches of life's purpose and explains the doctrine of Christ, which is central to that purpose.
Its message is plain: Christ is the center.
**The right hands for the work** A restorer needs permission to touch the work. God gave it through those who held the keys before.

The keys of the kingdom of God are committed unto man on the earth, and from thence shall the gospel roll forth unto the ends of the earth, as the stone which is cut out of the mountain without hands shall roll forth, until it has filled the whole earth.
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
Three of the original twelve Apostles—Peter, James, and John—restored the apostleship and keys of priesthood authority.
Heaven sent the same men who once walked with the Savior.
**A living work** The Church was organized in 1830. The work did not stop there. It goes on today.

And also those to whom these commandments were given, might have power to lay the foundation of this church, and to bring it forth out of obscurity and out of darkness, the only true and living church upon the face of the whole earth, with which I, the Lord, am well pleased, speaking unto the church collectively and not individually—

And in the days of these kings shall the God of heaven set up a kingdom, which shall never be destroyed: and the kingdom shall not be left to other people, but it shall break in pieces and consume all these kingdoms, and it shall stand for ever.
The First Presidency and the Council of the Twelve Apostles said this in the same proclamation. It is a proclamation, not a conference talk. It was read at the April 2020 general conference.
The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints, organized on April 6, 1830, is Christ's New Testament Church restored.
This is the Lord's Church, and you are invited in.

story.prompt: The member tells a true time about when they felt heaven was close. If the member has none, the app offers a story from the scriptures.
story.title: On the mountain

blocks.text: Peter, James and John saw Jesus with Moses and Elijah. Heaven and earth met on a mountain.

And after six days Jesus taketh Peter, James, and John his brother, and bringeth them up into an high mountain apart, And was transfigured before them: and his face did shine as the sun, and his raiment was white as the light. And, behold, there appeared unto them Moses and Elias talking with him.
The Restoration tells us this was not a one-time event. Heaven is still near. The same Apostles later returned to restore keys. When we pray, we are on a small mountain of our own.
